source_text:
11.8,9 Σὺ, Κύριε,
φυλάξεις ἡμᾶς, καὶ διατηρήσεις ἡμᾶς ... Κύκλῳ οἱ ἀσεβεῖς πε ριπατοῦσιν. ̓Επειδὴ ὁ
κύκλος τῇ εὐθείᾳ ἐναντίος ἐστὶ κατὰ τὴν σκολιότητα καὶ εὐθύτητα, οἱ δὲ ἀσεβεῖς
κύκλῳ περιπατοῦσιν, οἱ εὐσεβεῖς α ρα εὐθείαν περιπατοῦσι. ∆ιὰ τοῦτό φησι· Φυ
λάξεις ἡμᾶς, ἐπειδὴ κυκλοῦντες κυκλοῦσιν ἡμᾶς οἱ ἀσεβεῖς, ἐπιβουλεύοντες τῇ
ἡμῶν σωτηρίᾳ, ου τοι δ' α ν ει εν ἀντικείμεναι δυ νάμεις.
pass_a_gloss: You, Lord, you-will-keep us, and you-will-preserve us ... In-a-circle the ungodly walk. Since the circle to-the straight opposite is according-to the crookedness and straightness, the and ungodly in-a-circle walk, the pious then a-straight walk. Through this he-says: You-will-keep us, since circling they-circle us the ungodly, plotting to-the our salvation, these and would-be opposing powers.
pass_b_english: “You, Lord, will keep us, and you will preserve us … The ungodly walk in a circle” (Psalm 11:8-9).

Since the circle is opposite to the straight according to crookedness and straightness, and the ungodly walk in a circle, the pious then walk a straight [path]. Therefore he says: You will keep us, because circling they circle us, the ungodly, plotting against our salvation, and these would be opposing powers.

choices.why: Circle opposite to the straight as crookedness vs straightness. Not ‘they walk around the city walls’.
rejected: they walk around the city walls
they walk in a pious circuit

anf_compare.notes: ANF lacks this Greek catena as reading English.
